newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean hospital, subway workers to strike.
newsitem.headline: South Korean hospital, subway workers to strike.

text.p: Hospital and subway workers in South Korea announced they would join in nationwide industrial action in protest against the passage of a new labour law on Thursday.

More than 9,000 Seoul subway workers will strike on Saturday, a union statement said. So far unions at 13 medical institutions, including Seoul National University Hospital, the nation's leading medical facility, have decided to walk out on Friday, a union official said.

Unions at around 140 hospitals are affiliated to the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, which called an indefinite strike of all its members on Thursday, according to hospital union official Kim Gun-ye.
Many hospital unions were still debating industrial action, she said.

A statement by the union at the Seoul Metropolitan Subway Corp said the strike would start at 4.00 a.m. on Saturday (1900 GMT Friday), raising the prospect of transport chaos for tens of thousands of commuters who work a half day Saturdays. The statement did not say for how long the stoppage would last.
The subway union represents 9,300 of 11,232 subway workers in the South Korean capital.
